note: Authored findings before synthesis. Adult exclusion ratings align directly; pooled need-threat, mediation and downstream alcohol results are not exact-target evidence. Every record remains non-governed/NOT_ELIGIBLE.

findings.locator: Europe PMC PMC8924730: Participants, Cyberball, State Ostracism, Procedure, Results Table 2 and Limitations
findings.population: US Midwestern university undergraduates, mostly White/female; 2020 online study
findings.context: 30-throw virtual ball game with ostensible other players
findings.exposure: Other players stop passing to participant after initial inclusion
findings.measurement: Summed two-item ignored/excluded ratings, each 1–5; not actual toss percentage or a neural proxy
findings.timing: Immediately after game, retrospective to that game
findings.result: Exclusion condition reported higher ignored/excluded ratings than inclusion. FoMO and attachment-anxiety moderation terms were not detected; they were measured, not randomized.
findings.limitations: Participant exclusions and demand characteristics; no belief-in-human-players check, baseline mood absent, narrow young sample. No independent mediation or general social exclusion trajectory.

findings.locator: PMC11940692: Participants; Cyberball; Primary needs threat questionnaires, results
findings.sample: 50 adults in reported questionnaire contrast, 25 per condition
findings.context: 30-throw virtual game, initial inclusion then continued or stopped passes
findings.exposure: Stopped passes after initial common sequence
findings.measurement: Immediate felt-ignored rating, analyzed separately from needs-threat score
findings.result: Adults reported greater feeling ignored in the ostracism condition. No inference to attention performance or whole need profile is imported.
findings.limitations: Pseudo-random allocation, exclusions and small sample; questionnaire and video-coding samples differ; no chronic or clinical generalization.

findings.locator: PMC11940692: Results, Primary needs threat questionnaires; Discussion
findings.design: Age-six pseudo-random child protocol; separate younger-age scope
findings.sample: 40 children in questionnaire contrast; not the 39-person video-coding sample
findings.exposure: Stopped passes after initial common sequence
findings.measurement: Child felt-ignored item; comprehension/measurement comparability uncertain
findings.result: Age-six felt-ignored difference not statistically detected. Older children and adults differed; the younger-age result limits transport, not a demonstrated zero or within-adult contradiction.
findings.limitations: No equivalence margin; child questionnaire understanding may differ. OUTSIDE the proposed young-adult effect scope; not pooled with adults.

findings.locator: PubMed/Europe PMC abstract, Methods and Results statements
findings.design: Randomized intervention versus control after baseline assessment
findings.context: Computer-delivered comparative own/perceived/actual peer drinking feedback
findings.comparator: Control condition; exact content not extracted
findings.measurement: Perceived drinking norms; exact frequency/volume item specification not available in accessed abstract
findings.result: Reported perceived-norm changes, but accessed abstract does not resolve exact dimension/direction for the PSY-016 frequency/prevalence construct.
findings.limitations: Exact-target measurement and comparative feedback scope need full extraction. Behavior changes alone do not resolve this gap.

findings.design: Multisite randomized full PNF, partial social-comparison feedback and attention-control
findings.comparator: Partial own/actual comparison or attention-control; not interchangeable
findings.measurement: Perceived norms and drinking outcomes; exact norm item dimensions not extracted
findings.result: Consumption improved at three months in both feedback conditions; reported indirect associations included norms→later drinking and drinking→later norms. These do not independently establish either mediation route or a direct exact norm estimand.
findings.limitations: No transitive causal pathway, universal norm correction or requirement for one feedback component inferred; numerical effects not extracted.

findings.locator: PMC3440433 Discussion, Interpretation and Overall evidence
findings.population: UK university students; whole and higher-risk analyses
findings.context: Email normative feedback package with average-university referent
findings.comparator: Control groups under declared Solomon design
findings.measurement: Alcohol intake/AUDIT/problems, NOT direct perceived-norm outcome
findings.result: No detected improvement in downstream alcohol outcomes. This is not a null direct effect on PSY-016 and not an equivalence test.
findings.limitations: Different package/setting and low follow-up; downstream only. Retained as boundary evidence against automatic benefit or a presumed norm-mediated pathway.

assertions.scope: In the accessed young-adult virtual ball-game protocols, stopping passes after initial inclusion can increase immediate feelings of being ignored/excluded compared with continued inclusion. The claim is about perceived exclusion DURING THAT GAME, not chronic rejection, actual friendship loss, physiological stress or future behavior. Age-six non-detection is explicitly outside this proposed adult scope.
assertions.timing: Immediate post-game retrospective rating; no persistence estimate
assertions.measurement: Specified ignored/excluded self-report item(s), not toss-count accuracy, omnibus need threat or a neural measure.
assertions.mechanism: A configured interruption of expected participation provides cues interpreted as being ignored/excluded. Perception is measured as outcome, not treated as an independently randomized mediator.
assertions.rationale: Two independent publications provide aligned young-adult contrasts; one uses pseudo-random allocation and the other a narrow randomized student sample. The age-six null remains a transport limitation. No pooled effect size or universal effect is inferred.
assertions.contributionReconciliation: Alternative action-level description of the bounded exposure route underlying existing REL-SOC-062; no duplicate new Relationship or independent summation through an inferred belonging/stress pathway.
assertions.risk: Exclusion can cause distress. Research identity grants no permission to exclude, deceive or manipulate people; informed consent, debriefing, ethics, safety, legal authority and applicability must be independently evaluated.

assertions.scope: Research question: comparative feedback about own, perceived-peer and measured-peer drinking changes the exact PSY-016 prevalence/frequency judgment. Accessed abstracts support a norm-measure research direction but do not resolve volume-versus-frequency dimension, comparator detail or exact direction. Do not claim universal reduction or calibrated correctness.
assertions.timing: Study-specific 3/6-month norm assessments; downstream 6/12-month findings are separate
assertions.measurement: Exact reference-group, behavior frequency/prevalence and denominator item extraction REQUIRED; drink volume is not silently equated to frequency.
assertions.mechanism: Comparative information may update peer estimates or social comparison. Those routes are not separated by a regression-mediated result.
assertions.rationale: Preserve reported norm changes and alternative comparison mechanisms while withholding exact-effect readiness. UK downstream nondetection does not become direct norm null.
assertions.risk: No advice to disclose private drinking data, no universal truth/accuracy claim for survey norms and no automatic reduction in harm. Reference group, consent, privacy, stigma, feasibility and ethics unresolved.

happeningTypes.name: Withhold subsequent virtual ball passes after initial participation in a bounded inclusion task
happeningTypes.description: Configure computer-controlled co-players to stop passing to the participant after a declared initial inclusion sequence. This operation identity is not ostracism efficacy, a social-tie edit, a PSYWERX Relationship edit or practitioner permission.
happeningTypes.constraints: Potential distress/deception; consent, debriefing, safety and independent ethical/legal authority required. Distinct from real-group dissolution or existing SOC-F07 network assignment identities.

happeningTypes.name: Display a comparative own, perceived-peer and measured-peer behavior feedback panel
happeningTypes.description: Present a specified individual's report alongside their estimate of a declared reference group and an appropriately sourced estimate for that group. One comparative display operation; not a package of independent treatments. No accuracy, efficacy, behavior benefit or calibration promise.
happeningTypes.constraints: Actual reference-group data and provenance, privacy, consent, valid denominators, accessibility and risk assessment required; no fabricated norms. Different from claim repetition, refutation and network-referent message seeding.
